name: The Eighteenth Bed Collapse
summary: The attempt to hold the immortal border as a permanent crossing failed because a seat cannot be held by someone who cannot pay for it every period, and the abandoned crossing left a bed of unmortared seats at realm eighteen. It is why the border is still crossed one person at a time and why no sect has ever held it.

attributes.mechanism: upkeep claimed in arrears and never released
attributes.residue: a bed of unusable seats at realm eighteen
attributes.standing_prohibition: no sect may hold the crossing

name: The Refused Seating
summary: The attempt to seat a seventh law in a vacant slot, which cannot work, because a seat cannot hold what does not exist. The slot was consumed by the absence and thereafter cannot be told from an empty one. It is why only six laws are known, why the ledger stopped accepting additions, and why the vacant seats of the upper tiers are vacant rather than merely unfilled.

attributes.mechanism: a slot spent on a law that was never defined
attributes.standing_consequence: no tier can prove a vacant seat is empty

name: The Density Ceiling
summary: The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of the end of their own tier, and nobody has explained it since. The era that produced it is the era of a complete composition with no redundancy, which is the frame in which a fixed dense body has nothing left to form. The ceiling is still there and still unexplained by anyone who was not there.

attributes.surviving_account: one, and it is a stonecutter's

name: The Unfilled Ledger
summary: Nine vacant seats at the top, four in the tier below, and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty. It is why the highest tier is never drained but crowded, because unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep, and it is why the one faction holding two tiers will not give up the lower of them.

attributes.standing_effect: the highest tier's upkeep is paid by its own vacancies
attributes.present_question: which of the nine, if any, may be certified empty

name: The Unowned Genealogy
summary: At least one carrier line has no household willing to admit to it and a founding bar that no pairing can clear except one generation of pure inheritance, which is arithmetic rather than history. Whether it descends from the culled branches, from the crossings, or from nothing at all is unresolved, and the line that does hold the oldest surviving record still cannot prove its claim to be older.

attributes.evidence: one household's own record, contested by nobody able to disprove it
attributes.arithmetical_note: the bar is reachable by exactly one generation of pure pairing

name: The Branch Cull
summary: Houses that could not fund a cultivator's ascent culled their own branches instead, because a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster than the same line spread across a village, and a cull is the only way to stop paying for siblings. It is why the narrowed line exists at all, and why its grant favours sustained effort: the line was selected under debt, not designed.

attributes.consequence: a narrowed line whose grant is sustained rather than sudden

name: The Vacancy Decree
summary: The rule that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one, and that every appointment passes a trial the office cannot judge. It exists because the four vacant immortal seats were very nearly filled by decree, and that attempt is what taught this setting to write vacancy down as its own state rather than as a zero.

attributes.instrument: appointments routed through a trial the office cannot judge
attributes.origin: an earlier attempt to fill vacant seats by appointment

name: The Cinder Famine
summary: A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, so the fastest race in the setting was the shortest-lived and the most dominant at once. The famine was the demographic shape of that arithmetic: a population whose fuel is its own body, thinning at exactly the rate it could not stop.

attributes.mechanism: structural elemental affinity with no seated elemental law

name: The Iron Grief
summary: The mortal tier's only caging ore ran out at the seam, and a mortal world seats three laws and therefore has no spatial law to move its own size or open fresh rock. One exhausted seam so cost the tier its whole ladder: cores stopped forming, Nascent Soul became unreachable, and everyone standing above Foundation starved where they stood.

attributes.trigger: iron_ore seam exhausted on the Mortal Plains
attributes.compounding: no seated spatial law means no new seam can be opened

name: The Law Census
summary: The first time anyone counted laws against seats and got an answer that did not change. A law's tier list says where it may apply; a seat says where it is actually installed. So a law can apply to a tier and still have no seat in it, and the census is the reason mortals live under three of six laws without ever knowing three were missing.

attributes.method: seat-by-seat ledger of installed laws, cross-read against tier lists
attributes.census_result: 3 of 6 seated at the mortal tier
attributes.cost_of_the_method: three laws recorded as never installed, names retained

name: The Passage Ledger
summary: Because the cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, the one thing anyone can actually control between tiers is permission to pass. That is where the counting houses and the marshal's authority over the crossings came from: passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, and nobody may levy a seat.

attributes.economic_consequence: crossing tariffs become the only durable wealth
attributes.central_prohibition: a seat may not be levied

name: The Realm Nine Verdict
summary: Cultivators had been reading realm nine as a wall they failed to climb. The verdict established that it is a limit they were never issued: the mortal tier seats a life law, and that seat is already spent keeping plants and beasts coherent, which is precisely why no humanoid and no elemental form is admissible here. The tier did not defeat anyone. It declined to seat them.

attributes.verdict: the ceiling is composed, not political
attributes.side_effect: unspecialised bodies stop one gate short of the ceiling

name: Reading the Sixth Seat
summary: How a tier's composition was learned a second time: seat the last missing law, then diff what the tier newly permits, and argue about which result caused the other. The finding worth recording is negative. A spare seat is not capacity for a new path. It is the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed.

attributes.method: add one law, diff what the tier permits, keep both readings
attributes.key_finding: surplus seats buy observation, not new paths
attributes.why_it_matters: it is the whole reason the highest tier is the one a mind occupies

name: The First Breath
summary: Realms one and two, in a tier that seats three of the six laws and costs almost nothing to hold. It starts as a fuel-rationing problem: qi law bottoms out at 0.1, so a mortal world carries roughly enough qi to light a first breath and none to spare, and every later era is an argument about where the fuel is.

attributes.span: the opening age, to the appearance of the Core

name: The Broken Bridge
summary: Realm eighteen, the last spirit gate and the border into the immortal tier, where the cost of existing changes character: upkeep goes from half a unit to as many as five. Realm eighteen is therefore an economic bottleneck before it is a spiritual one, and most of the people who never reached it were below realm nine and never knew the border existed.

attributes.span: after the density ceiling, to the Eighteenth Bed
attributes.defining_pressure: a crossing that costs more than a life returns

name: The Full Composition
summary: The spirit tier completes, realms twelve to eighteen, in the one frame where all six laws are present and none is doubled, so the medium is exactly as large as the demand placed on it. It ends at realm seventeen, where a maximally dense fixed body can no longer form the cavity it needs, which is a composition result and not a discipline failure.

attributes.span: the Sixth Seat to the Broken Bridge
attributes.defining_pressure: no spare seat to stand outside on

name: The Gilded Core
summary: Realms three and four, when the ladder's first genuine bottleneck turned out to be metallurgy. Iron ore on the Mortal Plains is the only dense material in the mortal tier's resource list, a core has to be caged in something, so the third gate was a mining problem a long time before it was a spiritual one.

attributes.span: after the census, to the Iron Grief

name: The Hundredfold Body
summary: Realms five through nine, the whole remaining mortal ladder, closed by a limit nobody was fighting. A mortal world is capped at a hundred and admits only plants and beasts, so realm nine is a life-law ceiling and not a defeat. The last two mortal gates were shut from the inside, by the frame, and the people who proved that are the reason anyone now knows the ceiling is a law.

attributes.span: after the ascent, to the Realm Nine Verdict
attributes.ceiling_proof: life_law seated, spent on the intelligence ceiling at nine

name: The Nine Empty Seats
summary: The immortal tier's nine realms, and the arithmetic that shaped every office in them: ten seats, six laws, and nothing to put in four of them. Those four are not a shortage, they are surplus, and an era whose defining political fact is a set of unfilled high seats produces the only kind of authority that can be built without filling them.

attributes.span: after the Eighteenth Bed, to the Still Point
attributes.defining_pressure: authority with no seat to sit in

name: The Sixth Seat
summary: The spirit tier's opening, realms ten and eleven, marked by the first composition with nothing missing: six seats against exactly six laws. It also opened onto the first resources that cannot exist below it, which is what made the earlier ascent irreversible rather than merely attractive.

attributes.span: after the branch cull, to the reading of the Sixth Seat

name: The Still Point
summary: The transcendent tier's three realms, and the only composition in the setting with real slack: fifteen seats against six laws. It is the one frame where a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and time runs between ten and a hundred times faster, which is the mechanical content of holding a single thought longer than any civilisation has existed.

attributes.span: the Nine Empty Seats to the present

name: The Seating of the First Tier
summary: Someone had to pay to open a world at all, and the bill was written in law seats. Upkeep rises about fortyfold from the mortal tier to the transcendent one, and qi is the only law with a thousandfold range, so qi was the only currency that could fund a tier. Whoever paid opened a three-seat frame and could not afford a fourth seat. Every tier since is a receipt for the same payment.

attributes.unresolved_account: no surviving record names the payer

name: The Peak Ascent
summary: The answer to the Iron Grief was to leave. Spirit stone and jade ore sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it, so cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks and did not come back. The movement was economic before it was spiritual, and it is why the mortal tier's populations thinned instead of recovering.

name: The Naming of Homes
summary: The three paths were separated and each was handed the tier it already occupied, on the reasoning that a method belongs where it works. The reasoning was sound and the outcome was fixed: the naming read as choice, so for three ages nobody costed what a tier actually cost, and the shortest-lived path was handed the cheapest frame as though cheapness were its nature.

attributes.error: a method's required frame recorded as a preference
attributes.cost_of_the_error: the body path's confinement accepted as doctrine for three ages
